clue.text: Start of spring period living near the sea

parts.note: spring is reckoned to begin on 1 March, written MAR I with I as the Roman numeral one
a period is a time

explanation.surface: A season's beginning marks a stretch spent living by the coast.
explanation.walkthrough: The start of spring is a date: 1 March, written MAR I (MAR is the month abbreviation, I is Roman one).
explanation.definitionFit: Maritime describes things connected with or found by the sea, such as coastal peoples and climates.

clue.text: Advantage of new gadget occasionally raised

indicators.note: in a down answer, raised means the picked letters are written upwards, so reversed
occasionally means taking only every other letter of the words new gadget

parts.note: the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters of new gadget

explanation.surface: Someone gains an advantage when a new gadget is sometimes lifted up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Occasionally' takes the even letters of 'new gadget', E, G, D, E; 'raised' turns EGDE round in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Having the edge over a rival means holding a slight advantage or superiority.

clue.text: Australasian creature, small dog bearing problem shedding coat

indicators.note: bearing means carrying, so the dog holds the other letters inside it

parts.note: a Pom is a Pomeranian, a small dog

indicators.note: shedding its coat means the word loses its outer letters, first and last

parts.note: an issue is a problem

explanation.surface: An antipodean animal, a little dog with a problem of moulting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shedding coat' strips the outer letters from ISSUE, and 'bearing' has the Pomeranian carry the SSU that is left; 'problem' is not the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The possum is a tree-dwelling marsupial of Australia and New Zealand, so an Australasian animal.

clue.text: Voting system replaced by Germany during earlier scheming

indicators.note: replaced by says the voting system's letters are swapped out for Germany's letter

parts.note: previous means earlier
PR is proportional representation, a voting system
D is the international vehicle code for Germany (Deutschland)

explanation.surface: An electoral system was swapped for German rule during an earlier plot.
explanation.walkthrough: In PREVIOUS (earlier), PR (proportional representation) is replaced by D (Germany).
explanation.definitionFit: Devious and scheming both describe someone underhand who plots to get their way.

clue.text: Poet upset by rude poster for daily paper?

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means the poet's name is turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: T. S. Eliot, the poet
a troll posts rude or provocative messages online

explanation.surface: A poet is annoyed by an offensive message on a daily newspaper's forum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset' turns ELIOT upside down to TOILE in this down entry. 'Daily paper' looks like a newspaper; it is the paper used every day in the bathroom, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Toilet roll is paper that most people use daily, a playful take on a newspaper.

clue.text: Middle-Eastern food smell, stale smell mostly

parts.note: hum is British slang for a bad smell

indicators.note: mostly means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: must is a stale, mouldy smell

explanation.surface: A Middle Eastern dish gives off an odour, mostly a musty one.
explanation.walkthrough: HUM (a pong) plus MUS, which is MUST (a mouldy smell) with 'mostly' cutting its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Hummus is a chickpea and tahini dip eaten across the Middle East.

clue.text: Attractive-looking house with last of visitors inside

indicators.note: inside says those letters go into the house

parts.note: a house is a home
and means with, joining things

indicators.note: last of means only the final letter of visitors is used

parts.note: the last letter of visitors

explanation.surface: A fine-looking house has the last of its guests still inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Handsome describes someone or something good-looking, pleasing to the eye.

clue.text: Accent beginning to betray villain

indicators.note: beginning to means only the first letter of betray is used

parts.note: the first letter of betray
a rogue is a villain

explanation.surface: A villain's accent is the first thing to give them away.
explanation.definitionFit: A brogue is a strong regional accent, especially an Irish one.

clue.text: Spectacular performance from lawman originally cracking case

indicators.note: cracking means breaking into, so the letter goes inside

parts.note: a binder is a folder or case for papers

indicators.note: originally means taking the word's first letter

parts.note: the first letter of lawman

explanation.surface: A lawman makes a spectacular showing by first cracking a case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Originally' takes L from lawman, and 'cracking' breaks it into BINDER. 'Case' reads as a detective's case; it is a ring binder.
explanation.definitionFit: A blinder is British slang for an outstanding display, as in 'played a blinder'.

clue.text: Dutch women's energy tackling sport in retirement

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for women

indicators.note: in retirement means going back, so the pieces are read backwards

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy
F1, Formula One motor racing, with the 1 written as I

explanation.surface: Dutch women spend their energy on sport after retiring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dutch' looks like the nationality; in cockney slang 'my old Dutch' (short for duchess) is a wife. E tackling F1 gives EFI, and 'in retirement' sends it back to IFE.
explanation.definitionFit: Dutch is old cockney slang for one's wife, from 'duchess'.

clue.text: One burning brightly with enthusiasm, male consumed by drink

parts.note: spirit means enthusiasm or zest

indicators.note: consumed by means the male letter is swallowed inside the drink

parts.note: to lap is to drink, as a cat does

explanation.surface: Someone shines with zeal, but the man is eaten up by drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A spirit lamp is a lamp fuelled by methylated spirit, so a thing that burns with a bright flame.

clue.text: Learning from old comedian

definitions.meaning: first meaning: knowledge and good judgement
second meaning: Norman ..., the British slapstick comedian of mid-century films

explanation.walkthrough: Norman Wisdom was a British film comic of the 1950s and 60s.
explanation.definitionFit: Wisdom is accumulated learning and knowledge, and also the surname of a famous British clown.

clue.text: Order idle husband endlessly to get cheese

indicators.note: order means arrange, so these letters are put into a new sequence
endlessly means husband loses its final letter

explanation.surface: Tell your lazy spouse to go and get some cheese, again and again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endlessly' cuts the D from husband to leave HUSBAN, and 'Order' rearranges IDLE plus HUSBAN; 'Order' looks like a command to the husband.
explanation.definitionFit: Danish Blue is a strong blue-veined cheese from Denmark.

clue.text: Modernises Somerset ad, pushed back to some extent

indicators.note: pushed back points to reading the run backwards
to some extent means only part of the words is used, a run of letters inside them

parts.note: the letters SET AD PU run across the end of Somerset, all of ad and the start of pushed

explanation.surface: A Somerset advert gets modernised but delayed a little.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To some extent' picks SETADPU out of 'SomerSET AD PUshed', and 'back' reads it in reverse.
explanation.definitionFit: Updates is a verb meaning brings up to date, so modernises.

clue.text: Nun needs regularly to plug crucial US president

indicators.note: to plug means the letters fill a gap inside the other word

parts.note: key means crucial

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of nun needs

parts.note: the first, third, fifth and seventh letters of nun needs

explanation.surface: A nun needs to fill an important gap for an American president.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regularly' takes the odd letters of 'NuN NeEdS', NNED, and 'to plug' puts them into KEY.
explanation.definitionFit: John F. Kennedy was the 35th President of the United States.

clue.text: Take away from daughter leaflet about illegal drug

parts.note: E is slang for ecstasy
a tract is a short pamphlet or leaflet

explanation.surface: Taking a leaflet about illicit drugs off a daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaflet about illegal drug' reads as E, then the TRACT written about it.
explanation.definitionFit: To detract from something is to diminish or take away from its worth.

clue.text: Story about inspiring old cavalry soldier

indicators.note: inspiring means breathing in, so the old letter goes inside
about means turned round, so the story's word is read backwards

parts.note: a report is a news story

explanation.surface: A tale of an old cavalryman who motivated others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' turns REPORT round to TROPER. 'Inspiring' looks like 'motivating'; it means breathing in, so O goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A trooper is a private soldier in a cavalry or armoured regiment.

clue.text: Huge opera singer loses time sumo wrestling

indicators.note: loses means the time letter is dropped from the singer

parts.note: a tenor is an opera singer

indicators.note: wrestling means the letters of sumo grapple into a new order

explanation.surface: A huge opera singer runs out of time while doing sumo.
explanation.walkthrough: TENOR 'loses' T to leave ENOR; 'wrestling' rearranges SUMO to MOUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Enormous and huge are synonyms for something very large.

clue.text: Rather hungry, like Gregory perhaps?

parts.note: Gregory Peck, the film actor; perhaps flags him as one example
-ish is a suffix meaning like, somewhat

explanation.surface: Is someone who resembles a Hollywood star a bit hungry?
explanation.walkthrough: Gregory Peck was a Hollywood star; Peck-ish would mean like Peck.
explanation.definitionFit: Peckish is British for slightly hungry, wanting a snack.

clue.text: Favour wine European tourist on vacation tucks into

indicators.note: tucks into means those letters go inside the others

parts.note: rosé is a pink wine

indicators.note: on vacation means emptied, so only the outer letters of tourist remain

parts.note: the first and last letters of tourist

explanation.surface: A tourist on holiday enjoys a wine, with a European.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On vacation' empties tourist to TT. 'Tucks into' suggests eating but means going inside, and 'Favour' is a noun here, not a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A favour is a ribbon or badge worn as a token, as a rosette is.

clue.text: Lifting spirits essentially, that female South American monkey

indicators.note: essentially means the heart of the word, its central letter

parts.note: the middle letter of spirits

indicators.note: lifting says the spirits' heart is raised from the bottom of that female's word to the top in this down entry

parts.note: her refers to that female
US means American

explanation.surface: Raising the spirits of a female South American monkey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Essentially' gives R, the heart of spirits. 'Lifting' moves that R from the foot of HER to the top of this down entry, leaving HE below it, so RHE; then S and US.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhesus macaque is a monkey species, widely used in medical research.

clue.text: Tripped over in front of 9 Across's companion

parts.note: fell means tripped and went down
O is the cricket scoring abbreviation for an over
9 Across is wife, abbreviated W

explanation.surface: Someone tripped and fell in front of the wife's friend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tripped over' reads as one phrase; FELL is tripped and O stands for over, placed in front of W.
explanation.definitionFit: A fellow is a companion or comrade, as in fellow traveller.

clue.text: Understand TV chef supports what dieters should avoid

indicators.note: supports in a down entry means the chef's name sits below the other piece

parts.note: dieters avoid fat
Ken Hom, the television chef known for Chinese cookery

explanation.surface: A television cook backs what slimmers must steer clear of.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'supports' puts HOM beneath FAT. Ken Hom is a TV chef famous in Britain for his wok cooking shows.
explanation.definitionFit: To fathom something is to get to the bottom of it, to understand it.

clue.text: Killjoy that may ruin a picnic?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a person who spoils others' fun
second meaning, literal: a soaked rug laid on the grass would spoil an outing

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the literal reading of the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A wet blanket is an idiom for a gloomy person who dampens everyone's enjoyment.

clue.text: Search eastern half of underground tunnel system

indicators.note: eastern half means the right-hand half of the word, as on a map, so the first four letters go

parts.note: catacombs are underground burial tunnels

explanation.surface: Searching the east side of a subterranean network.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eastern half of' keeps the right-hand half of CATACOMB, since east is to the right in an across answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To comb an area is to search it thoroughly, as if with a fine-toothed comb.

clue.text: Mention spectacle on the radio

indicators.note: on the radio means as heard spoken, so the word is matched by sound

parts.note: a sight is a spectacle

explanation.surface: A spectacle is mentioned on a radio broadcast.
explanation.definitionFit: To cite something is to refer to or quote it, so to mention it.

clue.text: Disturbance of last month led by trade union members primarily

indicators.note: led by means the last-month piece comes after the others
primarily means taking the first letter of members

parts.note: first letter of members
ult., short for ultimo, means last month in formal letters

explanation.surface: Last month's unrest was led mainly by union members.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Primarily' gives M from members; ULT is 'led by' TU and M, so it comes last. ULT (ultimo) is the old business-letter abbreviation for last month.
explanation.definitionFit: A tumult is an uproar or commotion, a disturbance.

clue.text: Drive off to meet solicitor when one is facing penalties

parts.note: shoo means to drive away
a tout solicits custom, selling tickets or services

explanation.surface: Chase someone away before meeting your lawyer when facing fines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Solicitor' looks like a lawyer; it is one who solicits, a tout. A shoot-out settles a drawn football match by penalty kicks.
explanation.definitionFit: A penalty shoot-out is when each team's players face penalties in turn to decide a tie.
